Press Release:


uMhlathuze Water Board
Their mission is to provide sustainable and affordable water and improve the quality of life of people living in rural areas across KZN. But according to reports, the uMhlathuze Water Board has been spending its money on five-star hotels, business class flights and royal patronage. Despite qualified audits, audit reports and allegations of years of mismanagement, the splurging continued unabated.


Script:


The drought has made water an even more precious resource, but at the Department of Water and Sanitation money has also dried up. Last year, the department was given a R750 million cash injection by Treasury, which then implemented austerity measures. Managing our water in South Africa are our water boards - which operate regionally. In Kwa-Zulu Natal’s Richards Bay area, Mhlathuze Water provides purified bulk water for a tariff to the local paper and mining industries, and also to the municipality, which in turn distributes it to around 350 thousand people. Themba Mgwaba left the department of water affairs to come to Mhlathuze Water.
Themba: “I was a general manager of operations in 2005, to ensure that we expand Mhlathuze water business into the rural areas.”
In 2008 he started the Water and Sanitation for schools project - which supplies drinking water and ablution facilities to rural schools in KZN.
Themba: “There was going to be national elections, government was going to identify key projects, but it was just a special project.
Claire: “To highlight that things are happening?”
Themba: “Yes.”
Former Mhlathuze Water employee, Lindi, not her real name, says projects like these made a huge difference in the communities.
Lindi: “Initially they’d use the bushes to go to the toilets if they and some of the students, they’d bring their own water to school.”
LINK: “IT MAY SEEM LIKE A INSIGNIFICANT PLACE, BUT IT THE SMALL COASTAL TOWN OF RICHARDS BAY IN KZN, THAT THOSE WHO CONTROL WATER HAVE BEEN INVOLVED IN A POWER STRUGGLE THAT LINKS STRAIGHT BACK TO INFLUENCE OF NOW FORMER PRESIDENT JACOB ZUMA.”
Enter Duduzile or Dudu Myeni, the very same person responsible for the board of South African Airways and the airlines alleged decline. However, before she got to that position, she was appointed as the chairperson of Mhlathuze Water’s board in 2002.
Julius: “Under the tenure of dudu myeni at SAA, the carrier lost about 10 billion rand. She actually abused her authority, which is why we want her to be declared a delinquent director, so that she cannot serve on any other board.”
Myeni is opposing that delinquency application which will be heard later this year. In the meantime, Julius Kleynhans who manages the Organization for Undoing Tax Abuse - or OUTA’s Water Portfolio says while the country was focused on SAA, the big money, because of the drought, was being funnelled from the department of water and sanitation towards big water projects.
Julius Bite: “Water boards are big implementing agents for the DWS, so huge amounts of capital actually goes to water boards.”
Mhlathuze water is the cheapest water board in the country.
Julius: “If you have the right people in the right positions, this is a possibility to do tender fraud and have the right people that you want in those positions to get that money.”
Themba thought it strange when Myeni asked to be involved in project. His concern grew when Myeni allegedly made demands for contractors to be added to the list of tender applicants.
Themba: “She came to me and said she wanted me to put some people into the panel for facilitation of the project. I think that’s where I fell out.”
Myeni allegedly often added names to prospective tender lists. Lindi was shocked when, she says, Myeni asked her to actually call and invite certain people, outside Mhlathuze’s area, to tender for a project.
Lindi: “Sometimes the chairperson interfered in the program asking me to add some consultants. She gave me the numbers of those people who to call.”
Sasha:/Claire: “Is that normal?”
Lindi: “No.”
Sources allege Myeni interfered in other tenders, because she wanted them to go to different contractors. Mhlathuze Water was taken to court for attempting to cancel a R50 million contract. In the Judgement that was not in Mhlathuze Water’s favour, the Judge said of Mhlathuze Water’s conduct...
Judge: “Undoubtedly, the way in which the respondent exercised its rights as a local authority should be of grave concern to every tax payer in this country.”
Then in January this year we received a stack of leaked documents signed “concerned staff members,” alleging that Myeni was misspending the funds of Mhlathuze water.
The complaints had been sent in early 2017 to the KZN: Public Protector’s office, which were then sent on to the water and sanitation department in March, where they sat until October. Attached was a KPMG internal report from August 2015 which found that Myeni had failed to declare her relationship to a business partner who was awarded a tender by Mhlathuze Water.
Several documents allege that a combined R2 million of Mhlathuze Water’s Corporate Social Investment fund had been used by Mhlathuze Water irregularly between 2014 and 2016.
This fund is meant to uplift impoverished communities through educational programmes, skills and sports development, and to provide clean drinking water.
“Isaac”, not his real name, was a board member of Mhlathuze Water.
Isaac: “The CSI must be a contribution to a community, that you don’t benefit anything in return, because if you’re going to benefit, it becomes something else.”
The whistleblowers also alleged Myeni’s family members worked at Mhlathuze Water - we checked and found her ex-husband, Mandla Myeni is employed as a manager.
We delved deeper into the CSI budget and discovered these emails from 2014, which show Dudu Myeni requested a R30,000 donation from the CSI fund to pay for water and drinks to His Majesty King Goodwill Zwelithini’s wedding to his fifth wife, Queen Nompumelelo. The royals could hardly be considered as impoverished. The couple also asked for an annual donation to the reed dance and to the King’s birthday.
A year later, Myeni’s ex-husband approved R228,000 rands worth of bottled water for His Majesty’s birthday.
Isaac: “She’s not been responsible in terms of using public money in that regard.”
In the same year, R137,000 of the CSI budget was used to buy these laptop bags for a women’s dialogue conference. The money was paid to a promotions company which branded the bags - carrying gifts like makeup, pamper kits, travel or spa vouchers and hair accessories.
In response to the 2015 KPMG report, Mhlathuze’s water board implemented regulations for the use of CSI funds. Myeni, herself, signed off on them. But less than a month later, she APPEARED to have second thoughts.
During a meeting at Zimbali Lodge, board members questioned her apparent continued use of CSI funds for festivals and lunches: Myeni is alleged to have responded by calling for a review of those same CSI regulations. Lindi says Myeni ruled Mhlathuze Water with an iron fist.
Lindi: “She is very clever, because she’ll also study what kind of a person you are. She was like the queen of the jungle.”
And the splurge continued, with donations requests to local municipalities of R1.2 million for “furniture and entertainment” and R300,000 towards, so called, “mayoral activities.”
In 2015 the South African Association of Water Utilities - SAAWU - asked for R740,000 and 40,000 T-shirts for youth day celebrations in Soweto.
Mandla Myeni, as the acting CEO, authorised R500,000 for the T-shirts. Turns out Dudu Myeni has several positions at water associations – of which SAAWU is one.
LINK: “THESE TRAVEL REQUESTS DATING BACK TO 2010, ACCORDING TO MHLATHUZE WATER’S POLICY, THEY MUST BE SIGNED OFF BY THE MINISTER OR THE CEO, BUT IN THIS THICK STACK, NOT ONE HAS BEEN APPROVED, AND DUDU MYENI FLIES BUSINESS CLASS, AND STAYS IN 5 STAR HOTEL ACCOMMODATION, ALSO CONTRAVENING THE POLICY.”
The list of luxurious hotels includes the taj in cape town, the Beverly hills in Umhlanga and some of the top hotels in sandton.
And when Myeni arrives, she arrives in style, often in chauffeured limos and mercedes benzes.
Sometimes her trips would be booked in advance - like for Stockholm’s World Water Week - which cost R250,000. Myeni, didn’t pitch, because she was allegedly needed at her other job at SAA.
Claire: “Why didn’t any of the CEOs challenge any of the stories that were brought forward, were they true?”
Themba: “You challenged, you are gone.”
Themba was later suspended with pay for alleged misconduct. He believes the real reason was because he stood up to Myeni.
Themba: “I’m been suspended for refusing to do something that is wrong.”
Nine months later, another employee called him to a meeting with Myeni.
Themba: “Your investigation is finished and the report is very damning. Now chairperson as a motherly person, she would not like to see you suffering now
Claire: What’s going through your head at that point?
Themba: Where is the report and show me that it’s damning.. It exonerated me!”
After being reinstated by the CCMA, he was forced out again.
Temba: “At 12 o’clock midnight a guy called me. if you come back the only way of removing you is to silence you, so chief please, you have kids. CCMA called Mhlathuze, they were very happy they settled for two years salary.”
Julius: “If you look at the tactics they’ve used, a lot of key positions have been filled with acting roles, they actually try to suspend people without properly investigating them to get rid of them, and this is where the siphoning of money should take place.”
ADD BREAK
Themba and Lindi were just two of the many more casualties we were told about in this water board war, including 8 CEOs and other executives - anyone who stood in Myeni’s way.
According to court documents, one CEO, Sibusiso Makhanya, made the fatal error of allegedly refusing to sign off on a deal to implement trading stalls at Nkandla for R1.5 million. He was then suspended with pay.
Isaac: “There is a view, that seems to suggest that she is connected in higher places.”
Myeni allegedly never let anyone forget how close she is to Jacob Zuma.
Themba: “She can come into your office holding a phone talking to someone “yes baba Temba is in front of me, I’ll talk to him, yes baba” you know whom I’m talking to? I’m talking to baba. There was power behind.”
Claire: “Number 1”
Themba: “Once she drops his name, you won’t ask how high you should jump.”
Sources say her current house in the upmarket suburb of meerensee, in Richards Bay, is allegedly where former president Zuma spent some time. It’s also listed as the address of the Jacob Zuma Foundation - of which she is also the chair!
The Suspended CEO, Makhanya decided to fight back by taking the now former minister of water and sanitation, Nomvula Mokonyane to court. Since the recent cabinet reshuffle she has NOW become the new minister of communications, and reportedly left HER FORMER department bankrupt. In Makhanya’s court documents, he claimed Myeni has captured the Mhlathuze’s board.
LINK: “IN A DAVID VERSUS GOLIATH STORY, CEO SIBUSISO MAKHANYA FOUGHT FOR HIS SURVIVAL, AND IT ALL CAME DOWN TO THIS JUDGEMENT IN THE PMB HIGH COURT, WHICH WAS NOT ONLY SCATHING OF THE MINISTER OF WATER AND SANITATION NOMVULA MOKONYANE, BUT JUST LIKE IN THE STORY, MUCH TO EVERYONE’S SURPRISE, THE LITTLE GUY DEFEATED THE GIANT.”
Dudu Myeni’s rule was meant to end in 2015, after her three terms of office were up – but then Water and Sanitation Minister Mokonyane instead, extended the board’s term indefinitely.
The judgement however, effectively ended the board’s term, including Myeni’s time as chairperson. Makhanya then should have been reinstated. BUT Instead, in June 2017 Mokonyane disbanded the board entirely.
Interim CEO Mthokozisi Duze was then brought in from the Cooperative Government and Traditional affairs department or COGTA in June 2016 to replace the suspended Makhanya. When the board was dissolved, all executive power effectively fell to him.
Duze: “I am the current interim ceo, as well as the accounting authority as appointed by the minister, as MHL does not have the board currently.”
Isaac: “If the CEO is also the board, it means that he is a law to himself.”
Duze’s life hardly seems to leave space for his onerous responsibilities at Mhlathuze Water; He has several other businesses, and lives in Durban, which means he commutes to Richards Bay every week. To help him he has driver, a bodyguard, an assistant, and a secretary. We told him about some of the allegations made by the whistleblowers.
Duze: “This is called guillotine journalism you can’t ask a question on the hearsay basis, when you’re not given facts.”
LINK: “AS FAR BACK AT 2010 QUESTIONS WERE RAISED ABOUT MHLATHUZE WATERS’ FINANCIALS, IT WAS ONLY IN 2017 THAT THEY GOT THEIR FIRST QUALIFIED AUDIT.”
Duze: “They were more around matters of non-compliance with supply chain management policies, which if in the main, which could deem some transactions irregular, but its not fruitless expenditure.”
For his public service at the small water board, Duze is paid R2.2 million a year - more than our ex-president - and it comes with a performance bonus of R600,000. Despite austerity measures, a month after he became CEO, Duze flew to new york city as a representative of COGTA to attend a funeral that formed part of his duties at his previous position in disaster management. But this weeklong trip was paid for by Mhlathuze Water for R120,000. AND three months ago he spoiled over 40 Mhlathuze Water employees by taking them to Port Edward for R175,000 “strategic planning conference.” The spending continues, but Duze says Mhlathuze is financially healthy.
LINK: EVIDENCE IS MOUNTING… TIME TO ASK THE TOUGH QUESTIONS TO THOSE WHO ARE ULTIMATELY RESPONSIBLE.
After the interview in writing Duze said he would only respond to our allegations in a press conference.
We called Dudu Myeni on her number, which bizarrely used to belong to none other than Jacob Zuma. She said she would consider an interview as long as we sent her an email.
“Upsound.”
She has not responded to our detailed questions, neither has her ex-husband Mandla Myeni.
At the time of this interview, Mlimandlela Ndamase was the Ministerial spokesperson for Nomvula Mokonyane at the Department of Water and Sanitation before President Cyril Ramaphosa reassigned Mokonyane to the Department of Communications. Ndamase claimed the department and its now former minister had no knowledge of Myeni’s alleged conduct.
Mlim: “With the former chair as we have said until her term had concluded there was no allegation before us.”
Claire: But we’ve got documents from the public protector in KZN it asked the department to respond.
Mlim: “There’s no investigation by the department however PP as for the note you have put in front of me obviously if requesting support from the department and will receive that support.”
Claire: “It was received by your department in march and you hadn’t responded until October.”
Mlim: “Well it doesn’t clarify here on what information was requested but we could check with the relevant officials.”
We pointed out that the internal audit was attached.
Mlim: “Personally I am not aware of the KPMG report but we need to confirm what actions the department has taken.”
Claire: So if you find that there was no action taken.”
Mlim: “Those who may be found wanting or on the wrong side of the law may be brought to book accordingly.”
Apparently allegations supported by documents aren’t enough.
Mlim: “So the chair doesn’t operate as a tower excluded from the board of uMhlathuze.”
And what about the judgement regarding the suspended CEO where similar allegations were made against Myeni?
Mlim: “That judgement said the minister acted unlawfully in extending the term of the board and as I have said the minister on new legal advice took the decision not to appeal the judgment
Claire: “People find it hard to believe that the minister was not aware of these allegations.”
Mlim: “The minister has no business in protecting the former chair. The minister will fully support any investigation as long as it is led by credible legally mandated institutions. ”
Ndamase, said while he fully supports Duze’s leadership he will look into his spending habits.
Mlim: “We would be concerned because there are austerity measures in place…
As for the future of Mhlathuze, Mokonyane has gazetted its de-establishment, so that it can amalgamate with Durban’s Water Board. Although Treasury and the JSE questioned the merger back in 2015, the Ministry says it has engaged with all stakeholders. Although Mhlathuze’s website CURIOUSLY congratulates Myeni on her new role overseeing this process, Ndamase says it isn’t true.
Mlim: “She’s got no participation or role in the processes currently that are being processed by the department.’
Eight years after his ordeal Themba says he was never officially cleared by Mhlathuze and he has struggled to find work.
Themba: “My integrity is still intact, I’ve never done anything wrong.”
On Tuesday this week in parliament, it was decided that there will be an enquiry into allegations of maladministration and corruption at the Water and Sanitation Department under its former Minister Nomvula Mokonyane’s leadership. Then on Wednesday, Dudu Myeni was a no-show for a second time at the Eskom enquiry, which is investigating allegations that she had prior knowledge that 4 eskom executives would be suspended. It seems those in powerful positions may soon be forced to answer for at-least some of the allegations swirling around them.

Judge: “Undoubtedly, the way in which the respondent exercised its rights as a local authority should be of grave concern to every tax payer in this country.” Then in January this year we received a stack of leaked documents signed “concerned staff members,” alleging that Myeni was misspending the funds of Mhlathuze water. The complaints had been sent in early 2017 to the KZN: Public Protector’s office, which were then sent on to the water and sanitation department in March, where they sat until October. Attached was a KPMG internal report from August 2015 which found that Myeni had failed to declare her relationship to a business partner who was awarded a tender by Mhlathuze Water. Several documents allege that a combined R2 million of Mhlathuze Water’s Corporate Social Investment fund had been used by Mhlathuze Water irregularly between 2014 and 2016. This fund is meant to uplift impoverished communities through educational programmes, skills and sports development, and to provide clean drinking water. “Isaac”, not his real name, was a board member of Mhlathuze Water. Isaac: “The CSI must be a contribution to a community, that you don’t benefit anything in return, because if you’re going to benefit, it becomes something else.” The whistleblowers also alleged Myeni’s family members worked at Mhlathuze Water - we checked and found her ex-husband, Mandla Myeni is employed as a manager. We delved deeper into the CSI budget and discovered these emails from 2014, which show Dudu Myeni requested a R30,000 donation from the CSI fund to pay for water and drinks to His Majesty King Goodwill Zwelithini’s wedding to his fifth wife, Queen Nompumelelo. The royals could hardly be considered as impoverished. The couple also asked for an annual donation to the reed dance and to the King’s birthday. A year later, Myeni’s ex-husband approved R228,000 rands worth of bottled water for His Majesty’s birthday. Isaac: “She’s not been responsible in terms of using public money in that regard.” In the same year, R137,000 of the CSI budget was used to buy these laptop bags for a women’s dialogue conference. The money was paid to a promotions company which branded the bags - carrying gifts like makeup, pamper kits, travel or spa vouchers and hair accessories. In response to the 2015 KPMG report, Mhlathuze’s water board implemented regulations for the use of CSI funds. Myeni, herself, signed off on them. But less than a month later, she APPEARED to have second thoughts. During a meeting at Zimbali Lodge, board members questioned her apparent continued use of CSI funds for festivals and lunches: Myeni is alleged to have responded by calling for a review of those same CSI regulations. Lindi says Myeni ruled Mhlathuze Water with an iron fist. Lindi: “She is very clever, because she’ll also study what kind of a person you are. She was like the queen of the jungle.” And the splurge continued, with donations requests to local municipalities of R1.2 million for “furniture and entertainment” and R300,000 towards, so called, “mayoral activities.” In 2015 the South African Association of Water Utilities - SAAWU - asked for R740,000 and 40,000 T-shirts for youth day celebrations in Soweto. Mandla Myeni, as the acting CEO, authorised R500,000 for the T-shirts. Turns out Dudu Myeni has several positions at water associations – of which SAAWU is one. LINK: “THESE TRAVEL REQUESTS DATING BACK TO 2010, ACCORDING TO MHLATHUZE WATER’S POLICY, THEY MUST BE SIGNED OFF BY THE MINISTER OR THE CEO, BUT IN THIS THICK STACK, NOT ONE HAS BEEN APPROVED, AND DUDU MYENI FLIES BUSINESS CLASS, AND STAYS IN 5 STAR HOTEL ACCOMMODATION, ALSO CONTRAVENING THE POLICY.” The list of luxurious hotels includes the taj in cape town, the Beverly hills in Umhlanga and some of the top hotels in sandton. And when Myeni arrives, she arrives in style, often in chauffeured limos and mercedes benzes. Sometimes her trips would be booked in advance - like for Stockholm’s World Water Week - which cost R250,000. Myeni, didn’t pitch, because she was allegedly needed at her other job at SAA. Claire: “Why didn’t any of the CEOs challenge any of the stories that were brought forward, were they true?” Themba: “You challenged, you are gone.” Themba was later suspended with pay for alleged misconduct. He believes the real reason was because he stood up to Myeni. Themba: “I’m been suspended for refusing to do something that is wrong.” Nine months later, another employee called him to a meeting with Myeni. Themba: “Your investigation is finished and the report is very damning. Now chairperson as a motherly person, she would not like to see you suffering now Claire: What’s going through your head at that point? Themba: Where is the report and show me that it’s damning.. It exonerated me!” After being reinstated by the CCMA, he was forced out again. Temba: “At 12 o’clock midnight a guy called me. if you come back the only way of removing you is to silence you, so chief please, you have kids. CCMA called Mhlathuze, they were very happy they settled for two years salary.” Julius: “If you look at the tactics they’ve used, a lot of key positions have been filled with acting roles, they actually try to suspend people without properly investigating them to get rid of them, and this is where the siphoning of money should take place.” ADD BREAK Themba and Lindi were just two of the many more casualties we were told about in this water board war, including 8 CEOs and other executives - anyone who stood in Myeni’s way. According to court documents, one CEO, Sibusiso Makhanya, made the fatal error of allegedly refusing to sign off on a deal to implement trading stalls at Nkandla for R1.5 million. He was then suspended with pay. Isaac: “There is a view, that seems to suggest that she is connected in higher places.” Myeni allegedly never let anyone forget how close she is to Jacob Zuma. Themba: “She can come into your office holding a phone talking to someone “yes baba Temba is in front of me, I’ll talk to him, yes baba” you know whom I’m talking to? I’m talking to baba. There was power behind.” Claire: “Number 1” Themba: “Once she drops his name, you won’t ask how high you should jump.” Sources say her current house in the upmarket suburb of meerensee, in Richards Bay, is allegedly where former president Zuma spent some time. It’s also listed as the address of the Jacob Zuma Foundation - of which she is also the chair! The Suspended CEO, Makhanya decided to fight back by taking the now former minister of water and sanitation, Nomvula Mokonyane to court. Since the recent cabinet reshuffle she has NOW become the new minister of communications, and reportedly left HER FORMER department bankrupt. In Makhanya’s court documents, he claimed Myeni has captured the Mhlathuze’s board. LINK: “IN A DAVID VERSUS GOLIATH STORY, CEO SIBUSISO MAKHANYA FOUGHT FOR HIS SURVIVAL, AND IT ALL CAME DOWN TO THIS JUDGEMENT IN THE PMB HIGH COURT, WHICH WAS NOT ONLY SCATHING OF THE MINISTER OF WATER AND SANITATION NOMVULA MOKONYANE, BUT JUST LIKE IN THE STORY, MUCH TO EVERYONE’S SURPRISE, THE LITTLE GUY DEFEATED THE GIANT.” Dudu Myeni’s rule was meant to end in 2015, after her three terms of office were up – but then Water and Sanitation Minister Mokonyane instead, extended the board’s term indefinitely. The judgement however, effectively ended the board’s term, including Myeni’s time as chairperson. Makhanya then should have been reinstated. BUT Instead, in June 2017 Mokonyane disbanded the board entirely. Interim CEO Mthokozisi Duze was then brought in from the Cooperative Government and Traditional affairs department or COGTA in June 2016 to replace the suspended Makhanya. When the board was dissolved, all executive power effectively fell to him. Duze: “I am the current interim ceo, as well as the accounting authority as appointed by the minister, as MHL does not have the board currently.” Isaac: “If the CEO is also the board, it means that he is a law to himself.” Duze’s life hardly seems to leave space for his onerous responsibilities at Mhlathuze Water; He has several other businesses, and lives in Durban, which means he commutes to Richards Bay every week. To help him he has driver, a bodyguard, an assistant, and a secretary. We told him about some of the allegations made by the whistleblowers. Duze: “This is called guillotine journalism you can’t ask a question on the hearsay basis, when you’re not given facts.” LINK: “AS FAR BACK AT 2010 QUESTIONS WERE RAISED ABOUT MHLATHUZE WATERS’ FINANCIALS, IT WAS ONLY IN 2017 THAT THEY GOT THEIR FIRST QUALIFIED AUDIT.” Duze: “They were more around matters of non-compliance with supply chain management policies, which if in the main, which could deem some transactions irregular, but its not fruitless expenditure.” For his public service at the small water board, Duze is paid R2.2 million a year - more than our ex-president - and it comes with a performance bonus of R600,000. Despite austerity measures, a month after he became CEO, Duze flew to new york city as a representative of COGTA to attend a funeral that formed part of his duties at his previous position in disaster management. But this weeklong trip was paid for by Mhlathuze Water for R120,000. AND three months ago he spoiled over 40 Mhlathuze Water employees by taking them to Port Edward for R175,000 “strategic planning conference.” The spending continues, but Duze says Mhlathuze is financially healthy. LINK: EVIDENCE IS MOUNTING… TIME TO ASK THE TOUGH QUESTIONS TO THOSE WHO ARE ULTIMATELY RESPONSIBLE. After the interview in writing Duze said he would only respond to our allegations in a press conference. We called Dudu Myeni on her number, which bizarrely used to belong to none other than Jacob Zuma. She said she would consider an interview as long as we sent her an email. “Upsound.” She has not responded to our detailed questions, neither has her ex-husband Mandla Myeni. At the time of this interview, Mlimandlela Ndamase was the Ministerial spokesperson for Nomvula Mokonyane at the Department of Water and Sanitation before President Cyril Ramaphosa reassigned Mokonyane to the Department of Communications. Ndamase claimed the department and its now former minister had no knowledge of Myeni’s alleged conduct. Mlim: “With the former chair as we have said until her term had concluded there was no allegation before us.” Claire: But we’ve got documents from the public protector in KZN it asked the department to respond. Mlim: “There’s no investigation by the department however PP as for the note you have put in front of me obviously if requesting support from the department and will receive that support.” Claire: “It was received by your department in march and you hadn’t responded until October.” Mlim: “Well it doesn’t clarify here on what information was requested but we could check with the relevant officials.” We pointed out that the internal audit was attached. Mlim: “Personally I am not aware of the KPMG report but we need to confirm what actions the department has taken.” Claire: So if you find that there was no action taken.” Mlim: “Those who may be found wanting or on the wrong side of the law may be brought to book accordingly.” Apparently allegations supported by documents aren’t enough. Mlim: “So the chair doesn’t operate as a tower excluded from the board of uMhlathuze.” And what about the judgement regarding the suspended CEO where similar allegations were made against Myeni? Mlim: “That judgement said the minister acted unlawfully in extending the term of the board and as I have said the minister on new legal advice took the decision not to appeal the judgment Claire: “People find it hard to believe that the minister was not aware of these allegations.” Mlim: “The minister has no business in protecting the former chair. The minister will fully support any investigation as long as it is led by credible legally mandated institutions. ” Ndamase, said while he fully supports Duze’s leadership he will look into his spending habits. Mlim: “We would be concerned because there are austerity measures in place… As for the future of Mhlathuze, Mokonyane has gazetted its de-establishment, so that it can amalgamate with Durban’s Water Board. Although Treasury and the JSE questioned the merger back in 2015, the Ministry says it has engaged with all stakeholders. Although Mhlathuze’s website CURIOUSLY congratulates Myeni on her new role overseeing this process, Ndamase says it isn’t true. Mlim: “She’s got no participation or role in the processes currently that are being processed by the department.’ Eight years after his ordeal Themba says he was never officially cleared by Mhlathuze and he has struggled to find work. Themba: “My integrity is still intact, I’ve never done anything wrong.” On Tuesday this week in parliament, it was decided that there will be an enquiry into allegations of maladministration and corruption at the Water and Sanitation Department under its former Minister Nomvula Mokonyane’s leadership. Then on Wednesday, Dudu Myeni was a no-show for a second time at the Eskom enquiry, which is investigating allegations that she had prior knowledge that 4 eskom executives would be suspended. It seems those in powerful positions may soon be forced to answer for at-least some of the allegations swirling around them.
